A.explanation: These are multiples of $46\text{ Hz}$, giving half-integer multiples of $92\text{ Hz}$ such as $1.5 \times 92$. A node-antinode tube cannot support these.

B.explanation: These are $1, 2, 3, 4$ times $92\text{ Hz}$. Even multiples need a node-node or antinode-antinode tube, not a node at one end and antinode at the other.

C.explanation: Odd multiples $1, 3, 5, 7$ times $92\text{ Hz}$ give $92$, $276$, $460$ and $644\text{ Hz}$, which satisfy node at mouthpiece and antinode at open end.

D.explanation: Although $276\text{ Hz}$ is allowed, $828\text{ Hz}$ is $9 \times 92\text{ Hz}$ but $1288\text{ Hz}$ is $14 \times 92\text{ Hz}$, and even multiples are not allowed.

hints: Notice the boundary conditions stated: a displacement node at the mouthpiece and an antinode at the flared open end.
Recall how tube length $L$ fits quarter wavelengths for this node-antinode case: $L = \lambda/4, 3\lambda/4, 5\lambda/4$ and so on.
Since wave speed is fixed, check how frequency $f = v/\lambda$ scales from the $92\text{ Hz}$ fundamental when $\lambda$ takes those allowed values.
walkthrough: Identify the pipe type from the question: closed at the mouthpiece end with a node and open at the flared end with an antinode, so it behaves as a closed pipe.
For a closed pipe of length $L$, stationary waves satisfy $L = (2n-1)\lambda/4$ for $n = 1, 2, 3...$, so allowed wavelengths are $4L, 4L/3, 4L/5, 4L/7$.
With fixed sound speed $v$, frequency is $f = v/\lambda$, so frequencies are odd multiples of the fundamental $f_0 = v/4L = 92\text{ Hz}$.
Calculate the next harmonics: $3 \times 92\text{ Hz} = 276\text{ Hz}$, $5 \times 92\text{ Hz} = 460\text{ Hz}$, $7 \times 92\text{ Hz} = 644\text{ Hz}$.
The set $92\text{ Hz}$, $276\text{ Hz}$, $460\text{ Hz}$, $644\text{ Hz}$ matches the odd-harmonic series. This is option C.
